providers.claudeCode: 2.1.287 (isolated profile, model haiku, ask rules for nohup/sleep/touch)

summary: Claude: Bash approval reached the Loom card; Claude's own run_in_background job ran inside the run scope (host, claude, zsh, sleep); Stop ended it and the scope was verified empty with no stop failure.
Codex: the first approval reached the card and was answered there (file created); per-conversation server and TUI share one run scope; Stop emptied it.
Active work in both providers, window closed, normal Quit: succeeded, every scope empty, no active command or run host left, outside control process alive.

findingsFromRealRuns.REAL-1: Claude 2.1.287 stamps its initial registry status before startedAt; the tracker marked a normal flow as an ambiguous clock. Fixed (R2).
findingsFromRealRuns.REAL-2: Concurrent hook helpers and racing registry reads (out-of-order by ms, backwards or equal-ms samples) produced the same false Problem in a second conversation. Fixed: only rollbacks over 500 ms or future stamps are ambiguous; stale samples are ignored; a sample must be newer than every hook seen.
findingsFromRealRuns.driver: Real TUIs treat text plus an immediate Return as a paste; '/' opens Claude's completion menu; input before the TUI draws its prompt is lost. The driver sends Return separately until work starts and waits for readiness.
findingsFromRealRuns.codexDetachedJob: Codex reaps a command's own background children when the command ends, so a detached job could not be observed to outlive it; the server-escape case remains covered by the scoped fake-provider test (OWN-B1).
